dedupe_keys.name: sturm flood u net trained on sentinel 1 imagery

description: WEO publishes a pretrained U-Net for binary flood segmentation from Sentinel-1 synthetic-aperture-radar imagery. The model belongs to the STURM-Flood project, whose global benchmark uses 128-by-128-pixel tiles at 10 m resolution from 60 flood events. Zenodo resolves the model concept to version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15189665 and distributes a TAR.GZ archive under CC-BY-4.0, publicly and free. The companion GitHub notebook documents TensorFlow inference with Python 3.8 or later, producing water-probability and binary-mask GeoTIFFs and optional evaluation tables. The separately licensed inference code uses CC-BY-SA-4.0. Sensor preprocessing and performance outside the training distribution remain limitations; published weights do not establish operational flood-detection reliability. The model can create observed flood-extent estimates for comparison with hydraulic simulations and infrastructure exposure maps. It complements the Sentinel-2 model by using radar inputs. Weights were not downloaded and inference was not run.
